smells.finding: driver_utility_observable.py's _validate_inputs (lines 112-137) is a near-verbatim copy of regime_utilization.py's _validate_inputs (lines 193-220): same 4 checks (min-length, curvature/v_real/v_ideal length match, v_ideal finiteness) with nearly identical error message text, duplicated across the two sibling modules rather than factored into a shared helper (e.g. alongside the already-shared _build_regime_masks import). Not blocking -- does not affect correctness or the F4 no-ratio contract -- but a real ~25-line duplication worth extracting on a future touch of either module.

In scripts/build_driver_utility_observables.py, the identifier tuple (year, session_type, gp_name, round_idx[, constructor, driver]) recurs as separate keyword params across ~9 of the CLI's ~15 functions (_axis_row_exists, _error_row_exists, _driver_round_complete, _insert_error_row, _insert_axis_rows, _resolve_pending_drivers, _load_round_track, _process_constructor, _process_driver). A small context object (e.g. a RoundKey/DriverTask dataclass) would collapse this repeated clump, and would pay off further once G2/G3 extend the same schema. (Separately, the per-axis field group in RegimeDeficits -- g_*/n_points_*/sigma_lapsampling_*/mask_* x4 -- mirrors the sibling RegimeUtilization dataclass's established shape for the same 4-regime domain; that instance is NOT flagged -- see 'matches surrounding conventions', global-crew.md -- only the CLI's repeated identifier-tuple params are the flagged instance.) Not blocking -- purely a maintainability observation for a future gate.

_process_constructor and _process_driver each take con + 9-10 keyword-only params (11 total each) -- same root cause as the data-clumps finding above (the recurring year/session_type/gp_name/round_idx/constructor/driver identifier tuple). All params are keyword-only (named at call sites, not positional), which keeps call-site readability intact despite the count, so this is a minor, non-blocking observation rather than a real readability problem today.
